lifecycle:
DATA CONTRACT: spec.scope.exclusions (object, optional, nullable) {kinds: []string (<=50, each 1..63 chars, no '/'), resources: []{kind, name, namespace} (<=200, every field required)}. Absent == empty == no exclusions. CEL on scope: resources may be non-empty only when type == applications. Kinds are plain base kinds (Deployment, ConfigMap, ...); the renderer expands an excluded kind K, and the kind K of an excluded resource, to K plus K/scale when K is a base of ScaleSubresourceKinds, because Kyverno `*` and plain kinds never match subresource requests.

WHO WRITES IT: the UI through discovery Prepare/Update/Duplicate (Write + edit permission, closed end to end by the PERM plan); discovery writes the exporter with a service token (Internal). A session identity PATCHing exporter plans/protection/{id}/patch with {scope: {exclusions: ...}} is refused by GuardPlanLifecycle because `scope` is a lifecycle/material key (no list change).

RENDER: policies.Render(plan) -> for every rendered policy, for every rule, ExcludeResources.Any += ExclusionFilters(plan.Scope.Exclusions, scope.Namespace): one {kinds:[K(,K/scale)]} per excluded kind, one {kinds:[r.kind(,r.kind/scale)], names:[r.name]} per excluded resource whose namespace equals the scope namespace. Nil exclusions append nothing (byte-identical output). Same for Prepare, Activate, Reactivate, approve, health repair and the update combos path (subPlan now carries plan.Scope.Exclusions).

UPDATE TRANSITIONS (req.Scope.Exclusions nil = untouched, precedent req.TagIDs/EnvironmentID; non-nil = full replacement; {} or {kinds:[],resources:[]} = clear):
A. exclusions unchanged: today's combos diff; rendered sub-plans carry the stored exclusions.
B. exclusions changed and plan active: MaterialChange true -> approval gates as today (approved required active/scheduled => 400 ErrApprovedPlanMaterialEdit; pending => re-request in the same raw patch) -> ApplyFullRender(old plan, new plan): datapolicies.Render(new plan incl. new targets, policies, mode, exclusions) -> Deploy (SSA Force overwrites same names) -> exporter patch renderedPolicies = deployed -> only then DeletePoliciesByLabelAndNames(planID, oldRendered \ deployed). Coverage never dips: deploy precedes delete. On a Deploy or patch failure, RollbackFullRender deletes only attempted names absent from oldRendered and re-applies Render(old plan) filtered to oldRendered. The plan keeps its old policies and old exclusions, and the CR is unchanged.
C. exclusions changed and plan not active (scheduled, pending_approval, canceled...): no cluster call; the patch persists the new exclusions; the next Activate/Reactivate/approve renders the full plan.
D. persistence: BuildPatch sets patch.Scope (whole ScopeRequest with effective exclusions) whenever targets or exclusions changed; applyPatch goes raw whenever patch.Scope != nil and writes scope.exclusions explicitly as {kinds:[...], resources:[...]} (both arrays always present so merge patch replaces both) or JSON null when the effective value is empty (merge patch deletes the key). Stored CRs therefore never carry an empty exclusions object.

DUPLICATE: copied verbatim from the source (no override field). CANCEL/TERMINATE/CLEAR/REACTIVATE: untouched (their raw patches never touch scope). HEALTH: names only, unchanged; a content-only drift stays invisible (pre-existing ceiling, documented).

UI: FormValues.excludedKinds []string + excludedResources []string encoded `kind/namespace/name`; ScopeSection shows 'Excluded kinds' under both pickers and 'Excluded resources' under applications only; payload always sends scope.exclusions {kinds, resources} (resources [] for namespaces); snapshot, dirty detection and the active-plan re-render warning include both; details Scope card shows both rows when non-empty. Older UI bundles never send the key, so their edits leave stored exclusions untouched.

decisions.question: Where do exclusions live: a new top-level spec key or inside scope?
decisions.choice: spec.scope.exclusions, nested under the existing scope object (data ProtectionPlanScope.Exclusions *ProtectionPlanScopeExclusions, json exclusions,omitempty).
decisions.why: scope is already a material key in the exporter guard (constants/plans.go:20-24 lists `scope`; the guard checks top-level keys only, guard.go:266-285), is patched as a whole ScopeRequest by update (patch.go:78-85), copied by duplicate (duplicate.go:118-124) and compared by the UI scope predicates. Nesting means zero new guard keys, one CEL rule beside the union rule, and one place for everyone (incl. the APPS coverage derivation, which keeps reading scope.applicationIds/namespaces) to look.

decisions.question: How do exclusions reach the policy engine: filter the resources fed to templates, or add exclude filters?
decisions.choice: Append to every rendered rule's `exclude.any`: {kinds:[K(,K/scale)]} per excluded kind and {kinds:[kind(,kind/scale)], names:[name]} per excluded resource, applied once in policies.Render after each template renders (new internal/data/policies/exclusions.go).
decisions.why: Filtering ScopeSpec.AppResources cannot express the namespaces scope (BuildMatch emits MatchAllAny with the template kinds, often `*`, and no names: shared.go:277-279), does not touch BuildIdentityMatch (label selector, independent of AppResources: shared.go:195-211) and does not reach the PVC rule (VolumeClaims from the claim reader). The exclude list is an OR (`any`) that every rule already carries (ExcludePlatformWrites/ExcludeControllerWrites, shared.go:155-186), so one central append covers every template, both scopes and every future template. Kyverno acceptance is gated by the existing real-validator test (discovery tests/policies/kyverno_accepts_test.go), extended in S6.

decisions.question: Do exclusions change policy names?
decisions.choice: No. PolicyName hashes namespace + sorted app IDs only (shared.go:106-115); exclusions are content.
decisions.why: Same names let Applier.Deploy (SSA, Force=true, applier.go:31-63) overwrite rules in place, keep renderedPolicies/health bookkeeping stable and avoid a delete+create window. The price is that update must re-render on an exclusions change (next decision).

decisions.question: How does update apply an exclusions change to an active plan?
decisions.choice: New protpolicies.ApplyFullRender(old, new): render the whole new plan with datapolicies.Render and deploy it, then return the stale names (old names not re-rendered). Run deletes the stale names only after the exporter patch succeeds. Both failure paths (Deploy error, patch error) call RollbackFullRender: it deletes only the attempted names absent from the old renderedPolicies and re-applies Render(old plan) for the old names. Used only when exclusions changed; otherwise the combos diff stays (with subPlan now carrying exclusions).
decisions.why: The combos diff never re-renders unchanged (policy,target) pairs (orchestrator.go:64-71), so an exclusions-only edit would deploy nothing. Worse, renderCombos renders one app per sub-plan (deployment.go:53-75) so its names differ from the create/activate/repair grouped names (renderer.go:72-103) for multi-app-same-namespace plans: a per-app re-render would leave the grouped policy enforcing without the exclusion. Full render uses the same path as Prepare/Activate/repair, converges naming as a side effect, and is ~30 lines beside ApplyClusterDiff. Deploy-then-delete keeps the existing 'coverage never dips' order. The existing failure cleanups cannot be reused. A full render reproduces the live names (D3), so ApplyClusterDiff's deploy-error cleanup (cluster_diff.go:47) and RollbackPatchFailure (cluster_diff.go:86) would each delete the plan's whole enforcement.

decisions.question: How is an exclusions edit persisted and cleared through the exporter merge patch?
decisions.choice: req.Scope.Exclusions nil = untouched (precedent: req.TagIDs / req.EnvironmentID in patch.go:59-62, :93-97); non-nil = full replacement. BuildPatch sets patch.Scope whenever targets or exclusions changed, carrying the effective exclusions; applyPatch goes raw whenever patch.Scope != nil and writes scope.exclusions as {kinds:[...], resources:[...]} (both arrays present) or JSON null when empty.
decisions.why: MapToJSONPayload drops nil pointers and omitempty-empty slices (rest/mappers/payload.go:41-43, :78-93, :120-124) and JSON merge patch (kcore patch.go:27, exporter handler.go:100-141) keeps absent keys and merges nested objects, so a typed patch can neither clear the object nor empty one of its arrays. The raw route already exists for the approval re-request (orchestrator.go:117-133). Nil-means-untouched also keeps older UI bundles from clearing exclusions on every edit.

decisions.question: Are exclusions a material change?
decisions.why: They change what is rendered. Everything else follows from the existing predicate: approved required active/scheduled plans refuse the edit (ErrApprovedPlanMaterialEdit), pending plans re-request approval in the same raw patch, the UI ACTIVE_SCOPE_WARNING fires (scopeItemsChanged extended). No new lifecycle code.

decisions.question: Which permission gates editing exclusions?
decisions.choice: The plan edit permission and its deny rule, nothing new: exclusions are a scope field on the existing update route, behind the existing exporter `scope` guard key, inside ScopeSection whose `disabled` prop and the toolbar/card Edit gate already govern scope.
decisions.why: The PERM plan is designed so that a new spec option is covered by the edit permission without a special case; this feature is that option. The pre-existing gap (discovery update route requires Write but not Denyable(editprotectionplan), requirements.go:55-67) is PERM's to close; this plan adds no authz code and no route.

decisions.question: Where does the UI get kinds and resources to pick from?
decisions.choice: Applications scope: kinds = keys of resourceSummary with count > 0 across the selected apps from the Redux applications list (already loaded by usePlanFormData via fetchAllApplicationsThunk); resources = fetchApplicationDetails(name) per selected app, called directly (not fetchApplicationDetailsThunk) and cached per app in a new hook. Namespaces scope: kinds = the 14 fixed keys of DEFAULT_RESOURCE_SUMMARY (exported from applicationMapper.ts). No new endpoint.
decisions.why: No endpoint lists kinds per namespace, and the fixed summary vocabulary is exactly the set of kinds the templates enforce on (WorkloadKinds, ConfigMap/Secret, PVC, HPA...). The list endpoint strips resources (list.go:43-47; mapper forces resources: []), so per-app details are the only resource source; dispatching the thunk would clobber the single applications.details slot used by the application details page (models/application.ts:377-380).

decisions.question: How are excluded resources represented in the antd form?
decisions.choice: String keys `kind/namespace/name` in FormValues.excludedResources with encode/decode helpers in planFormValues.ts; decoded into {kind,name,namespace} objects in buildPreparePayload.
decisions.why: antd multi-Select values are strings; the three fields cannot contain '/'. Keeps FormValues flat like applicationIds/namespaces and the snapshot sortable.

decisions.question: Validation bounds and where they are enforced?
decisions.choice: kinds <= 50 (plans.ExclusionKindsMax), resources <= 200 (plans.ExclusionResourcesMax), kind/name/namespace required on each resource, resources only for applications scope. Enforced in the CRD (maxItems, maxLength, required, CEL), discovery validation.Exclusions (called from validation.Scope for Prepare/Duplicate and from update.validateRequest), and exporter Validate/ValidatePatchScope (resources-vs-type only, for direct callers).
decisions.why: CRD bounds are the persisted contract and fail loudly (422) if a service ships before the chart; discovery gives the UI a readable 400; the exporter check is two small funcs beside the existing union checks so a direct PATCH cannot land an inconsistent scope. Kinds are not validated against a vocabulary server-side: an unknown kind renders a harmless exclude entry.

decisions.question: Backward compatibility?
decisions.choice: Absent exclusions -> nil -> Render appends nothing (test asserts rendered policies deep-equal today's output). Existing CRs untouched; older UI bundles never send the key so their edits leave exclusions untouched; older discovery/exporter images ignore the key on read (data struct without the field drops it) and the exporter would prune it on write only if the CRD chart is older than the image, hence rollout order telark-crds -> exporter -> discovery -> UI.
decisions.why: Required by the brief; the pointer + nil-means-untouched pair is what makes both directions safe.

decisions.question: Duplicate semantics?
decisions.choice: Exclusions are copied verbatim from the source; DuplicateProtectionPlanRequest gains no override.
decisions.why: Scope and policies are inherited on duplicate today (duplicate.go:43-74); the copy edits them afterwards through Update if needed.

decisions.question: How do EXCL steps share a Go module with PERM steps in the merged schedule?
decisions.choice: One lane per Go module across the three plans, PERM first: internal/data PERM:S1 -> S2; exporter PERM:S2 -> S4; discovery PERM:S3 -> S5 -> S6. internal/rest (S3) and the charts (S1) belong to EXCL alone, and APPS touches no Go module. The edges are recorded as `crossPlanDependsOn` (JSON) / **crossPlanDependsOn** (step headers). `dependsOn` stays plan-local, so every id in it exists in this plan. The PERM plan must carry no dependency on an EXCL step, or the merged graph gets a cycle. Each step's verify runs only its own packages. Module-wide go build/test/golangci-lint runs only in the integrated V gate, after that module's lane drains. A failure in a file the step did not touch is reported to the orchestrator, never fixed in the step. dashboard-ui cannot be package-scoped, so U1/U2 follow the same report-not-fix rule and V4 is the zero-error gate.
decisions.why: File-level serialization is not enough. S2 and PERM S1 share no file, and neither do S6 and PERM S3; S5/PERM S3 and S4/PERM S2 were ordered only by a shared README. Every one of these steps leaves its module compile-red during test-first (S2: plans.ProtectionPlanScopeExclusions undefined; S6: protpolicies.ApplyFullRender undefined; PERM S1: roledata.ActionViewProtectionPlans; PERM S3: authz.RejectPlanRequirement). Meanwhile `go test ./...` and golangci-lint typecheck every package of the module, including tests, so the partner step's gate would go red mid-schedule and its agent would "fix" work that is not its own. PERM goes first because its steps are smaller and depend on nothing in EXCL. The cost is small. Only S2 (and through it S3 and U1) now waits, on PERM S1, which is one rules file plus its test. The other pairs were already serialized by a shared file. Package-scoped verifies also keep the Local AI Analyzer's in-flight edits (discovery insights, internal/data GlobalConfig) out of this plan's gates.

internal/data: `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint run` green; serialization test proves absent exclusions omit the key and a populated object round-trips; policies tests prove ExclusionFilters output, K/scale expansion, namespace filtering, and that Render of a plan without exclusions is deep-equal to today's output for every template in both scopes.

phases.goal: Exclusions are validated, persisted on create/duplicate, treated as material on update, rendered on every deploy path, and cleared through the raw patch.
acceptanceCriteria: services/discovery: `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint run` zero issues; every existing test passes unchanged.

tests/planvalidation: Exclusions rejects >50 kinds, >200 resources, empty/slashed kind, resource missing a field, resources on namespaces scope; accepts nil, kinds on both scopes, resources on applications.
